questions.question_text:
A hot pie cools according to $T=65e^{-0.06t}+18$, where $T$ is in degrees Celsius and $t$ is the number of minutes since it was placed on a bench.
What is its initial temperature?

options.why: Ignored the $+18$ in the model when substituting $t=0$.
Used the eventual temperature instead of the initial temperature.
Subtracted $18$ from $65$ instead of adding it.

questions.question_text:
A machine's value is modelled by $A=15\,000(0.88)^{t}$ dollars, where $t$ is the number of years since it was bought.
What is its value after $3$ years, to the nearest dollar?

options.why: Subtracted $12\%$ of the original $\$15\,000$ three times, treating the decay as a constant amount each year.
Used an index of $2$ instead of $3$.
Used an index of $4$ instead of $3$.

questions.question_text:
A sample of an isotope has mass $M=500(0.5)^{\frac{t}{8}}$ grams, where $t$ is the number of days since it was measured.
After how many days is the mass $62.5$ g?

options.why: Solved for $\dfrac{t}{8}$ and gave the number of halvings instead of the number of days.
Gave the time for one halving, which takes the mass only to $250$ g.
Used $\dfrac{1}{16}$ of the original mass rather than $\dfrac{1}{8}$.

questions.question_text:
The height of a spring is modelled by $h=7\cos t+11$, where $h$ is in centimetres and $t$ is in seconds.
What is its minimum height?

options.why: Added the amplitude to the mean position, giving the maximum height.
Gave the mean position instead of subtracting the amplitude.
Used the minimum of $7\cos t$ but ignored the vertical translation of $11$ cm.

questions.solution_text:
The minimum occurs when $\cos t=-1$.
$h=7(-1)+11=4$ cm.

questions.question_text:
A kettle of water cools according to $T=72e^{-0.03t}+24$, where $T$ is in degrees Celsius and $t$ is in minutes.
What is its initial temperature?

options.why: Ignored the $+24$ in the model.
Subtracted $24$ from $72$ instead of adding it.
Gave the eventual temperature instead of the initial temperature.

questions.question_text:
Waves have a maximum height of $14$ m and a minimum height of $2$ m, and their motion repeats every $12$ seconds. At $t=0$, the height is at the mean position and increasing.
Which model $y=k\sin(at)+c$ describes the height in metres after $t$ seconds?

options.why: Used the full difference between the maximum and minimum as the amplitude instead of half the difference.
Used $\pi/12$ instead of $2\pi/12$ as the coefficient, giving a period of $24$ seconds.
Used the minimum height as the mean position instead of averaging the maximum and minimum.

questions.solution_text:
$k=\dfrac{14-2}{2}=6$
$c=\dfrac{14+2}{2}=8$
$a=\dfrac{2\pi}{12}=\dfrac{\pi}{6}$
The height starts at the mean position and increases.
$y=6\sin\left(\dfrac{\pi t}{6}\right)+8$

questions.question_text:
The depth of water in a bay is modelled by $h=2\cos\left(\dfrac{\pi t}{5}\right)+6$, where $h$ is in metres and $t$ is the number of hours since high tide.
How long is the time between successive high tides?

options.why: Used the time from high tide to low tide, which is half the period.
Used the amplitude as the period.
Used the mean depth as the period.

questions.solution_text:
The time between successive high tides is the period.
$\text{Period}=\dfrac{2\pi}{\pi/5}=10$ hours.

questions.question_text:
The depth of water in a river is modelled by $h=10+4\sin\left(\dfrac{\pi t}{6}\right)$ for $0\le t\le12$, where $h$ is in metres and $t$ is in hours.
At which two times is the depth $8$ m?

options.why: Solved $\sin(\pi t/6)=1/2$ instead of $-1/2$, finding when the depth is $12$ m.
Used the times of maximum and minimum depth instead of solving for a depth of $8$ m.
Set the sine term to zero, finding times when the depth is $10$ m.

questions.solution_text:
$8=10+4\sin\left(\dfrac{\pi t}{6}\right)$
$\sin\left(\dfrac{\pi t}{6}\right)=-\dfrac{1}{2}$
For $0\le t\le12$, $\dfrac{\pi t}{6}=\dfrac{7\pi}{6}$ or $\dfrac{11\pi}{6}$.
$t=7$ or $11$ hours.

questions.question_text:
The depth of water in a bay is modelled by $d=3-\cos\left(\dfrac{\pi t}{4}\right)$, where $d$ is in metres and $t$ is the number of hours since low tide.
For how long between successive low tides is the depth at least $2.5$ m?

options.why: Found the total time below $2.5$ m instead of the time at or above it.
Gave the first boundary time instead of the duration between the two boundary times.
Gave the second boundary time instead of subtracting the first boundary time.

questions.solution_text:
The period is $\dfrac{2\pi}{\pi/4}=8$ hours.
$2.5=3-\cos\left(\dfrac{\pi t}{4}\right)$
$\cos\left(\dfrac{\pi t}{4}\right)=\dfrac{1}{2}$
For $0\le t\le8$, $\dfrac{\pi t}{4}=\dfrac{\pi}{3}$ or $\dfrac{5\pi}{3}$.
$t=\dfrac{4}{3}$ or $\dfrac{20}{3}$ hours.
The depth is at least $2.5$ m between these times.
Duration: $\dfrac{20}{3}-\dfrac{4}{3}=\dfrac{16}{3}$ hours.
